title: Session-anchored prefix merklestore for cross-request deduplication
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a compact, session-anchored Merkle-backed prefix index (the 'merklestore') that deduplicates prefix fragments across concurrent and sequential requests while preserving GPU residency invariants and continuous-batching performance. The merklestore will produce stable fingerprints for prompt segments, support partial/overlapping prefix materialization, and provide fast membership proofs for reuse decisions without full deserialization on the hot path.
design_notes: Use content-addressed chunking: break prefixes into variable-sized content chunks (heuristic boundary by token type + logits context) and compute per-chunk SHA-1-like fingerprint stored in a Merkle DAG for quick ancestry checks.

Session anchoring: map ephemeral session IDs to top-level merkle roots so multi-turn chat and related requests can share provenance while still allowing cross-session read-only reuse with lower trust credit.

GPU residency: store lightweight fingerprint ledger and compact reference counts in GPU-resident slab; actual KV values can be staged lazily into GPU memory when proof of reuse is accepted by scheduler.

Continuous batching compatibility: integrate lightweight proof verification hooks into the batch assembler so batch-level reuse can be decided pre-dispatch without serializing full segments into host memory.

Eviction interaction: coordinate with slab allocator through a 3-tier residency state machine (resident, resident-stub, evicted) to avoid IO storms when many batches request the same cold prefix simultaneously.
Fallbacks: on fingerprint collision or missing proof, fall back to existing prefix-materialization path and schedule an asynchronous reconciliation job to reconcile merkle entries.
Security/consistency: include canonical normalization of tokenization and prompt metadata into fingerprinting; maintain a monotonic proof-version to detect stale reuse across model upgrades.
APIs: provide read-only verification API for the runtime and write-through API for request ingress that records new merkle roots and updates reference counts atomically.

Trade-offs: Merkle proof ops add CPU hashing cost; we optimize by batching proof checks and using incremental hashing for append-only prompt fragments. Expected net win when reuse rate > 6% for 1k+ token contexts.
Metrics to track: proof hit rate, false positive collision rate, average extra CPU per proof, GPU page-in latency for resident-stub transitions, and overall token cost delta.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Proof-of-concept in experimental runtime: implement merkle chunker and on-disk store, expose proof verify API. (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Integrate GPU ledger: add compact fingerprint ledger in GPU slab and resident-stub states, test residency transitions. (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Batch assembler hooks: add pre-dispatch proof checks, measure impact on continuous-batching latency. (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Canary deployment on low-traffic tenant: evaluate reuse rates, collision profile, and eviction behavior. (2 weeks)
Phase 5: Rollout with telemetry dashboards and automated fallback thresholds. (1 week)
acceptance_criteria: Merklestore verifies membership proofs in <= 1.5ms median on canary hardware for 512 token fragments.
End-to-end reuse reduces average per-token GPU computation by at least 8% for the targeted canary workload compared to baseline without merkle reuse.
No regression in 95th percentile latency for production-like batching patterns (within 5% of baseline).
Eviction storms are prevented: resident-stub transitions remain under 200ms 95th percentile under simulated hot-cold churn.
Collision rate < 1e-9 for merkle fingerprints across 10M unique prefix fragments in testing harness.
Instrumentation: dashboards live with proof_hit_rate, proof_latency, gpu_pagein_latency, collision_alerts, and an automatic rollback trigger when proof_false_positive exceeds threshold.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: hashing CPU becomes a new bottleneck for small requests. Mitigation: batch hash operations; use incremental hashing and offload infrequent large-chunk hashing to background workers.
Risk: complex eviction logic may introduce correctness bugs. Mitigation: implement strict state machine tests and a reconciliation job that validates ledger vs slab snapshot nightly.
Risk: merklestore DB growth. Mitigation: implement TTL and GC policies keyed by last-accessed and tenancy; compress older subtrees into compact blobs.
Risk: model upgrades change tokenization leading to stale fingerprints. Mitigation: include tokenizer-version in fingerprint namespace and support multi-version lookup with conservative fallback.
Risk: tenant-specific privacy concerns for cross-session reuse. Mitigation: honor tenant isolation flag; cross-tenant reuse disabled unless tenant-level opt-in.

notes: Do not conflate merklestore with full KV materialization — merklestore is a fingerprint/proof layer designed to short-circuit heavy host<->GPU transfers when safe.
We will iterate on chunk boundary heuristics after we have real reuse telemetry; early defaults should bias for smaller chunks to increase match probability at the cost of metadata size.
Plan to run A/B with runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.21 to quantify end-to-end unit economics (token cost vs latency).
